energy.summary: Grounded in World Monitor’s Sep 9 crawlable pulse (latest published snapshot as of Sunday 13 Sep; live MCP/API still needs Balu’s WM auth). Brent $99.45 (+1.56%), WTI $94.31 (+1.38%), US hub nat gas soft (−1.2% to $2.88). The premium is Hormuz and Gulf security, not a US gas story. Distillate retail prints were not in the public quote panel.
cascadingImpacts: US–Iran / Hormuz → crude premium → headline inflation path
bullets: Brent $99.45 and WTI $94.31 on the Sep 9 WM quote panel.
Hormuz disruption 70/100 (Red); week-over-week transit movement −14.3% where published.
Saudi energy-site Houthi strike headlines in the country feed; UAE says exports will not be ‘held hostage’.

Ukraine stays Critical (UA 84). Yemen High (74) with Houthi/Iran-backed Gulf threat copy. UK/EU/Canada settlement sanctions hit Israel (IL 56, Falling −14).

Ukraine Critical 84; Iran High 73 Rising +4; Russia High 77.

food.summary: No FAO index print in the public pulse quotes. Transmission is still freight + war-risk insurance via Kerch (Azov grain) and Red Sea/Suez, not a harvest headline.
cascadingImpacts: Kerch/Red Sea risk → grain and food freight with a lag

transport.summary: Aviation and maritime sit on the same corridor map. UAE feed: Dubai/Abu Dhabi flight cancellations after Heathrow outage and fresh Iran strikes. Chokepoint board is the other half of delayed boxes.
cascadingImpacts: Chokepoints + Gulf strikes → ships and aviation → delayed boxes

UAE headlines tied flight disruption to Iran strikes and a Heathrow outage.

logistics.summary: Logistics is the wire between war and prices: Hormuz/Kerch/Suez red, Bab el-Mandeb yellow, Cape congestion High as an alternate. Transit counts missing on several Red straits (partial coverage), so scores are pressure signals, not closure certificates.
cascadingImpacts: Tanker/war-risk → freight inflation → CPI with a lag
bullets: Hormuz −14.3% and Bab el-Mandeb −10.7% week-over-week movement where published.
Cape of Good Hope congestion High on the same snapshot.

demographics.summary: No new UN/census print in the pulse. Displacement and labor stay in longer horizons until a WM demographics or UNHCR panel moves. Structural ageing unchanged.
cascadingImpacts: Displacement / labor → policy and growth capacity on 2y–5y
bullets: No fresh demographics series in the Sep 9 crawlable pulse.
Sudan crisis page still shows a severe fatality pulse (1,064 in the Aug HAPI/HDX month) — humanitarian, not a labor print.

public_policy.summary: Geopolitics board this week is war + trade policy, not a fresh CPI table: Trump escalates Canada tariffs/bans; UK/EU/Canada sanction Israeli settlement trade. German inflation rose with few energy-shock spillover signs (DE feed). FOMC 15–16 Sep remains the calendar event from the prior brief’s regime — not re-quoted on this pulse. Live FedWatch/CPI panels need authenticated WM access.
cascadingImpacts: War premium + tariffs → inflation expectations → G10 policy path
bullets: US–Canada tariff/ban escalation on the Sep 9 US developments feed.
UK + eleven European countries and Canada: settlement-product sanctions on Israel.
Authenticated WM MCP/API not connected this run — no fresh FedWatch print pulled.

base: Hormuz stays contested; Brent holds a three-digit neighborhood while Red scores persist.
FOMC 15–16 Sep is the near policy event; G10 still in a war-premium inflation regime.
Ukraine stays Critical on the instability board.
Risk assets chop around war headlines and the Fed meeting.
risks: Hormuz closure or mine scare lasting more than a news cycle — diesel and Europe gas, not just Brent.
Policy surprise at FOMC if live CPI/FedWatch (not in this pulse) has shifted.
Secondary Houthi hits on Saudi energy sites widen the Gulf premium.

base: Oil war premium fades only with a secure Hormuz corridor or ceasefire.
Trade rewiring via the Cape stays a freight cost, not a one-week detour.
Core inflation does not make a clean run at 2% while energy and tariffs bite.
Growth slows from the energy tax more than from a 2020-style collapse.
risks: Second-round inflation if food freight and diesel stick.
Europe winter gas if LNG routing around contested corridors stays ugly.
Policy error — too slow on headline war inflation, too fast on labor.

base: 2026 Hormuz/US–Iran shock remembered as a mid-cycle supply break.
Capex gravitates to energy, grids, and secured minerals.
Chokepoint politics stay on the standing risk board.
risks: Real recession if tightening and oil run together.
Frozen Gulf conflict that institutionalizes high-$80s to ~$100+ oil as normal.
Trade around the Cape for years, not weeks.

base: Chokepoint politics and mineral security become standing features.
Demographics and public debt cap any 1970s policy replay.
Mining and refining capacity, not ore in the ground, set the resource constraint.
risks: A wider great-power war that takes the dashboard off monitor.
A clean peace plus productivity burst that collapses the war premium.
This brief would then look hawkish in hindsight.

cascadingImpacts: US–Iran war → Hormuz/Kerch/Suez disruption → crude premium → headline CPI · inflation expectations → G10 policy path
Tariffs + settlement sanctions → trade friction → freight and food inflation with a lag
